lead: OpenAI's mathematics catalogue dominates the day, with 722 manuscripts at different stages of verification. Mistral Large 4 arrives, AI-assisted software copying raises ownership questions, and a streaming-fraud case ends in prison.

sections.title: Mistral Large 4 arrives
sections.intro: A preview, independent scores, and what Mistral is promising for the weights.

sections.title: OpenAI's maths flood and new API
sections.intro: 372 results from an internal model, and the Decisions API with a plugin to match.

sections.title: Cyber risk, open models and attacks
sections.intro: Banks in South Korea, vulnerability counts, and the case against banning open weights.

sections.title: Tools, models and money
sections.intro: Image models, embeddings, agent tooling, and funding.

sections.title: Arguments about intelligence
sections.intro: An open letter to Steven Pinker.

sections.title: Mathematics meets scrutiny and personal stakes
sections.intro: OpenAI publishes its catalogue, a roundup records the claims and caveats, and a researcher describes what it feels like to see a longstanding problem apparently solved. Publication and proof verification are different steps.

sections.title: Whose code, whose work?
sections.intro: Photopea faces unofficial AI-modified copies while an essay separates the technical, artistic and political objections to AI coding.

sections.title: Bots turn streams into stolen royalties
sections.intro: A prison sentence puts the distinction between synthetic songs and fraudulent listening in focus.

sections.title: Buying products and squeezing compute
sections.intro: Repeat acquirers drive AI deal counts higher; Turba Labs pitches data-center optimization, though only an excerpt of that funding report was accessible.

sections.title: Agents across devices, servers that earn their keep
sections.intro: NanoMuse describes a device-and-relay architecture, while a community thread asks what makes an always-on personal server worth maintaining.

sections.title: Games become a conversation
sections.intro: Google opens Playground while announcing a future professional route with Unity Spark.

sections.title: Agents enter files and business sessions
sections.intro: Claude adds Workspace editing, Hark ships software, and Sierra proposes a common way to connect personal agents with businesses.

sections.title: Cyber access and emergency response
sections.intro: Anthropic expands vetted cyber tiers, Project Zero examines emergency patch delivery, and console modders accelerate their work.

sections.title: Learning, trust and the teen-safety dispute
sections.intro: A junior engineer defends independent judgment, an essay examines manufactured consensus, and evaluators dispute whether teen safeguards work.

sections.title: Data, images and cluster recipes
sections.intro: Pantheon prioritizes diverse robot data, Google publishes an image model card, and NVIDIA pins tested cluster configurations.

sections.title: DeepSeek, recruiting and a new funding scale
sections.intro: Reported financing and benchmark gains sit alongside researcher recruitment challenges, a large venture-fund target and Stuut's enterprise automation raise.

sections.title: A phone camera finds the stars
sections.intro: AstroHelm uses on-device star-pattern matching to guide telescopes and telephoto lenses without a motorized mount.
